events.event: Pullman rolls out the first railroad dining car, the Delmonico, on the Chicago & Alton between Chicago and Springfield; dining cars are staffed by Black cooks and waiters.
events.evidence: NYHistory: 'In 1868 George Pullman... rolled out the first railroad dining car. It was dubbed the Delmonico... ran on the Chicago and Alton Railroad between Chicago and Springfield, Illinois.'

events.event: The first Black Pullman porter is hired, beginning the Black railroad service workforce.
events.evidence: Durbin (1969): 'The first Negro porter was hired in 1870.'

events.event: Elijah McCoy patents the automatic steam-chest locomotive lubricator (U.S. Patent 129,843), born of his work as a fireman/oiler on the Michigan Central.
U.S. Steel's Gary Works begins producing steel; the integrated mill (coke ovens, blast furnaces, open-hearth furnaces, rolling mills) draws Black Great Migration labor.
events.evidence: Gary Works production began 1908; Gary Black population 340 (1910) to 5,500 (1920).

events.event: Robert Crawford, 17, builds a fully functioning wireless station (homemade transmitter, receiver, telegraph key) while at Wendell Phillips High School; identified as the only Black member of Chicago's local Wireless Club

1919 steel strike: companies bring 30,000-40,000 Black and Mexican American workers into the mills; in Chicago, the race riot engulfs the Stockyards district and Black packinghouse workers are escorted in by state militia on August 8.
events.evidence: Wikipedia '1919 General Steel Strike'; Halpern (Cambridge) on Aug 8, 1919 militia escort.

events.event: Sam Taylor founds Taylor Electric in Chicago, described as the first Black-owned construction company in the city.
Ford Chicago Assembly (Torrence Avenue) begins production with the Model T.
Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters founded, August 25, under A. Philip Randolph.
Steel Workers Organizing Committee (SWOC) Local 1010 formed at Inland Steel, Indiana Harbor; William Young among original members, elected vice-president of merged Lodge 1010 in January 1938.

BSCP wins recognition from the Pullman Company, August 25 — first Black-led union contract with a major U.S. corporation; Memorial Day Massacre in South Chicago (10 killed) during the Little Steel strike.
Black electricians of IBEW Charter 9362 attain full membership in Chicago's IBEW Local 134.
NACA establishes the segregated West Area Computing unit at Langley; Dorothy Vaughan hired into it.
Dorothy Vaughan becomes the first African-American supervisor at NACA, heading the West Area Computing unit.
Katherine Johnson hired as a human 'computer' at NACA Langley, assigned to the West Area Computing section.
Bill Putnam's Universal Recording moves to 46 E. Walton St.; Malcolm Chisholm enters the industry under Putnam — the nursery for Chicago's blues-recording engineers
Universal releases half-speed-mastered discs on Mercury (1956); studio 'firsts' include tape repeat, the vocal booth, early 8-track, delay lines
Chess moves to 2120 S. Michigan; studio designed by audio engineer Jack Weiner opens late 1957 as Sheldon Recording Studios
NACA becomes NASA; segregated facilities, including the West Computing office, are abolished.
Chess takes control of the 2120 studio (Sheldon subsidiary) and hires Malcolm Chisholm from Universal Recording
events.evidence: City of Chicago Chess landmark report

events.event: Chisholm leaves for California; Ron Malo replaces him and builds dual echo chambers in the basement
events.evidence: City of Chicago Chess landmark report

events.event: NAACP report documents 'almost total exclusion' of Black workers from construction apprenticeships (60 of 9,360 electrician apprentices Black).
John Glenn's orbital flight proceeds after Katherine Johnson hand-verifies the IBM 7090's computed trajectory.
WVON launches on 1450 AM (1,000W day/250W night); a young Larry Langford serves as reporter/engineer
Chess buys the 8-story factory at 320 E. 21st St.; move completed late 1966/early 1967; becomes a vertically integrated record factory
events.evidence: City of Chicago Chess landmark report

events.event: Pullman Company ceases sleeping-car operation, December 31, 1968, ending the porter era.

Chicago Tribune (May 11) describes the 320 E. 21st St. plant: eight-track stereo tapes → vinyl master discs → nickel-plated stampers → records mass-produced, jacketed, packed, shipped in one building; 'performance to record shop in 24 hours'
events.evidence: City of Chicago Chess landmark report quoting Chicago Tribune

events.event: Mary Wallace becomes the first female CTA bus driver (State Street/36A route, July 9, 1974).
events.evidence: Face2Face Africa; Connecting the Windy City (citing Chicago Tribune).
events.source: Face2Face Africa; Connecting the Windy City

events.event: Ron Hardy starts DJing at Chicago gay club Den One with two turntables, a mixer, and a reel-to-reel tape deck
WVON moves 1450→1390 (5,000W ex-WNUS); Midway Broadcasting's WXOL launches on 1450 (1979)
Black Data Processing Associates (BDPA) founded by Earl Pace (Philadelphia); becomes a key pipeline for Black computing careers
events.evidence: Named in McIlwain's Black Software as a Black professional computing organization; founding year 1975 is widely cited but not re-verified from a primary source this pass
events.source: Theory, Culture & Society review of Black Software

events.event: Fairchild releases the Channel F, the first home video game console with interchangeable game cartridges; Jerry Lawson led the engineering team that adapted the prototype
events.evidence: Google Arts & Culture / The Strong National Museum of Play; artifacts include 1975 prototype boards and 1976 Math Quiz cartridge

events.event: Richard Long & Associates (Studio 54's system designer) installs the Warehouse sound system; Knuckles uses its crossover as a performance instrument
events.evidence: Robert Williams interview, Chicago Magazine (2018-08); disco sound-system scholarship

events.event: Emmit McHenry founds Network Solutions, Inc.; the company becomes the first domain-name registrar, central to the development of the DNS
events.evidence: Wikipedia (Emmit McHenry): founded 1979, first company to register domain names

events.event: Jerry Lawson leaves Fairchild and founds Video Soft, one of the first Black-owned video game development companies, producing software for the Atari 2600
events.evidence: Google Arts & Culture / The Strong: Video Soft founded 1982

events.event: Larry Sherman buys the Music/Musical Products pressing plant in Bridgeport and begins pressing records
Roland releases the TR-909 drum machine; after commercial failure and discontinuation (1985), it is adopted by Chicago house and Detroit techno producers as the genre-defining instrument
Jesse Saunders & Vince Lawrence record 'On and On' on a Tascam 4-track with TR-808 and Korg Poly 61; Sherman presses it at his plant; Trax founded

Marshall Jefferson buys his first rig (QX1, JX-8P, EX-800, TR-707, TR-808, Boss mixer, Tascam PortaOne 4-track, TB-303 for $150); Derrick May sells Frankie Knuckles a Roland TR-909, which Knuckles wires into the Power Plant club mixer
events.evidence: Jefferson interview, MusicRadar; Knuckles interview, RBMA 1995

events.event: Phuture (DJ Pierre, Spanky, Herb J) buy a second-hand TB-303 for $40; Pierre's live knob-twisting jam becomes 'Acid Tracks'
Mr. Fingers' 'Can You Feel It' cut by Larry Heard in one pass on Juno-60 + TR-909 bounced between two cassette decks (Trax); Jefferson's 'Move Your Body' piano laid at 40bpm, sped to 120bpm
Phuture's 'Acid Tracks' released on Trax; given to Ron Hardy on cassette as 'In Your Mind' and broken at the Music Box
Akai releases the MPC60, designed with Roger Linn; it becomes the standard beat-making instrument of hip-hop
AfroNet BBS active in the late 1980s, one of the earliest documented Black digital community networks
events.evidence: McIlwain via Marketplace: 'a bulletin board group called the AfroNet that sprang up in the late '80s'

events.event: NetNoir launches as an AOL channel for Afrocentric music, sports, education and business news, founded by E. David Ellington and Malcolm CasSelle
events.evidence: Futurity: 'dreamed up NetNoir, a stylish portal... made available to AOL subscribers'; McIlwain marketplace interview places NetNoir among high-profile mid-90s Black web companies

events.event: Farai Chideya launches Popandpolitics.com, 'one of the world's earliest blogs'

Latanya Sweeney re-identifies Massachusetts Governor William Weld's 'anonymized' medical record, launching modern data-privacy research; leads to k-anonymity and changes to HIPAA-era de-identification practice.
events.evidence: Harvard Magazine (Nov 2024) and Harvard Online accounts of the Weld experiment.

events.event: Ford and the EEOC sign a $7.75M settlement over sexual and racial harassment at the Chicago Assembly and Stamping plants.
Omar Wasow founds BlackPlanet, one of the first large-scale identity-based social networks; Myspace's founders were later quoted in Businessweek as having studied BlackPlanet as their model
Kanye West produces the core of JAY-Z's The Blueprint on an Ensoniq ASR-10 sampler (with MPC 2000 and Roland VS-1880 in his home-studio workflow), defining the 'chipmunk soul' Chicago production era
events.evidence: Just Blaze's Instagram post identifying the ASR-10 used during the Dynasty/Blueprint/BP2/Black Album sessions at Baseline (HotNewHipHop; Hypebeast, 2021)

events.event: Pew Research Center's first study of Black Twitter overindexing: 26% of African Americans online used Twitter vs 19% of whites online
events.evidence: Andscape: 'In October 2009, the Pew Research Center released the first study of black people overindexing on Twitter'

events.event: Timnit Gebru begins organizing what becomes Black in AI after counting few Black attendees at NeurIPS 2016; Joy Buolamwini founds the Algorithmic Justice League.
events.evidence: The Gradient profile of Gebru; AJL founding reported in multiple biographies of Buolamwini.

events.event: EEOC announces up to $10.125M Ford settlement after finding cause on harassment of female and Black employees at the Chicago plants.
First Black in AI workshop held at NeurIPS (Long Beach); Rediet Abebe and Timnit Gebru are the organization's founders; Data for Black Lives founded by Yeshimabeit Milner and Lucas Mason-Brown.
events.evidence: Black in AI Wikipedia history; D4BL Wikipedia (formation November 2017).

events.event: Gender Shades published (Buolamwini & Gebru): commercial facial classification error rates of 0.8% for lighter-skinned men vs. up to 34.7% for darker-skinned women.
events.evidence: MIT Technology Review Innovator profile of Buolamwini.

events.event: 'Ghost Work' (Mary L. Gray & Siddharth Suri) documents the hidden human data-annotation and content-moderation labor behind AI; Ruha Benjamin publishes 'Race After Technology: Abolitionist Tools for the New Jim Code.'
events.evidence: Publishers Weekly review of Ghost Work (2019); Princeton research news on Race After Technology (June 2019).

events.event: Raji's audit of Amazon Rekognition documents gender and racial bias in the product, intensifying pressure on Amazon; Amazon was hostile to the findings.
events.evidence: ZDNet interview with Raji; racismandtechnology.center summary.

events.event: IBM and Amazon pause or restrict police sales of facial recognition amid the audit findings, employee activism, and racial-justice protests; 'Coded Bias' documentary (dir. Shalini Kantayya, featuring Buolamwini and Raji) premieres.
events.evidence: Wikipedia (Deborah Raji) on IBM/Amazon decisions; documentary coverage.

events.event: December 2, 2020: Timnit Gebru's exit from Google over the 'stochastic parrots' paper; ~2,700 Google employees and 4,300+ academics sign in support; Black in AI, Queer in AI, and Widening NLP refuse Google funding in protest (2021).
events.evidence: thebluf.news account; Black in AI Wikipedia.

events.event: Jason Parham's Wired feature 'A People's History of Black Twitter' documents the community's origins (early hashtags #twitterafterdark, #youknowyoureblackwhen) and its role in memes and #BlackLivesMatter
events.evidence: RogerEbert.com review summarizing the piece; Hulu 3-part adaptation (2024)

events.event: Klassen et al. publish 'More than a Modern Day Green Book' (CSCW), a peer-reviewed interview study framing Black Twitter as a modern Green Book
December 2, 2021: Gebru founds the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR).
events.evidence: Ford Foundation interview with Gebru; thebluf.news.

events.event: Marian Croak inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame (one of the first two Black women) for VoIP inventions.
Microsoft retires face-based gender classification in Azure Face API, acknowledging problems with inferring such attributes; Buolamwini publishes 'Unmasking AI.'
events.evidence: Secondary summaries of Gender Shades industry impact.

events.event: ChatBlackGPT launches on Juneteenth (June 19, 2024) as a culturally informed AI platform for Black and African American perspectives; Nvidia names its flagship AI-training GPU architecture 'Blackwell' after David Blackwell.
events.evidence: CRN on ChatBlackGPT launch; eurweb on Nvidia naming.

events.event: Marian Croak and Moustapha Cisse named to TIME's 100 Most Influential People in AI (2026).
